## Background

::: {.question}
Data-Driven Differential Diagnosis in Human Genetics
:::

::: {.step-card}
**Today's talk**<br>
How human genetics uses data science and genomics to support differential diagnostics
:::

::: {.step-card .goal}
**The diagnostic rate** in human genetics has improved by roughly **300%** in the last two decades
:::

::: {.step-card}
**Our example**<br>
A patient with a Mendelian mimic of inflammatory bowel disease^[chronisch-entzündliche Darmerkrankung (abgekürzt CED)]
:::

## IBD: Rare and common

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="55%"}
![](./img/ibd-rare-and-common.jpg){.shadow-img fig-align="center"}
:::::

::::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.step-card}
**Common**<br>
Intestinal infections that nearly everyone gets once in a while
:::

::: {.step-card}
**Crohn disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC)**<br>
Together termed inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), ca. 1:200 individuals
:::

::: {.step-card .goal}
**Rare**<br>
Inborn errors of immunity (IEI), monogenic diseases that can present with IBD-like immunopathology, often severe and early-onset
:::

:::::

::::::

::: {.tiny-credit}
image: Uhlig HH. Monogenic diseases associated with intestinal inflammation: implications for the understanding of inflammatory bowel disease. Gut. 2013  PMID: 24203055.
:::

## IBD: Pathophysiology

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="42%"}
![](./img/ibd-pathophysiology.jpg){.shadow-img fig-align="center"}
:::::

::::: {.column width="58%"}

::: {.step-card}
**The model**<br>
Key intestinal defence functions and cellular immune regulation components are impaired in monogenic disorders with an IBD-like phenotype
:::

::: {.step-card .warn}
**The defects**<br>
Epithelial barrier and response, neutrophil numbers, phagocytosis and bacterial killing, and gut innervation. Together they increase bacterial translocation across the epithelium and bacterial survival
:::

:::::

::::::

::: {.tiny-credit}
image: Uhlig HH. Monogenic diseases associated with intestinal inflammation: implications for the understanding of inflammatory bowel disease. Gut. 2013  PMID: 24203055.
:::

## Rare in common

::: {.question}
Is "common disease" always what it seems?
:::

::: {.step-card .goal}
**70 of 1480 (4.73%)** participants with IBD, from five clinical trials, had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in a relevant gene
:::

::: {.step-card .warn}
**31 of 33** of those with a rare disease-causing variant showed no or only a short-term response to adalimumab, a TNF-α inhibitor approved by the FDA for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
:::

::: {.step-card}
In clinical practice, rare forms of common disease may be difficult to recognize. **Misdiagnoses of rare diseases as common ones are not infrequent.**
:::

::: {.small-text}
* [Rahimov F, et al. (2025) Common Diseases in Clinical Cohorts - Not Always What They Seem. _N Engl J Med_ **393**:1589-1598](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41124632/)
* [Robinson PN (2025) A Rare-in-Common Paradigm for Precision Genomic Medicine. _N Engl J Med_ **393**:1648-1649](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41124636/)
:::
